standard.title: Interpret information, ideas and opinions in texts
standard.description: interpret information, ideas and opinions in a range of spoken, written and multimodal texts, and respond appropriately to cultural context, purpose and audience
standard.prior_knowledge: Students can locate and process information across multiple sources and respond in varied ways (AC9LS6C03). They have not yet evaluated source reliability, interpreted humour and cultural nuance, or compared perspectives across diverse community contexts.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students interpret information, ideas and opinions in a range of target language texts — evaluating source reliability, responding to cultural nuance and humour, and responding appropriately to context, purpose and audience.

nodes.label: Evaluating sources and interpreting opinion
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can evaluate the reliability and accuracy of target language information sources and express opinions about text content.
nodes.minimum_width: Evaluate at least one source for reliability using at least one explicit criterion; share at least one opinion about text content using appropriate language.
nodes.typical_width: Access and evaluate information sources for reliability and accuracy; compare different source types for validity and perspective; share opinions on topics of interest to young people; express agreement and disagreement with authors; exchange preferences and perspectives on characters and events in imaginative texts.
wider: Compare the same event covered in two different target language sources — identify where they agree, where they diverge, and explain what the divergence reveals about each source's perspective
Evaluate a target language social media post on a factual topic — identify specific indicators of reliability and explain the evaluation criteria used
nodes.hinge_reason: Source evaluation is the prerequisite for the synthesis and evaluation demands of subsequent bands. Students who accept all sources at face value cannot synthesise across multiple perspectives or recognise that texts serve particular purposes.

response_modes.reason: Source evaluation requires explicit criteria and reasoning — students need to articulate what makes a source credible or biased before they can apply this spontaneously.

success_criteria: Evaluates at least one source for reliability using at least one explicit criterion
Shares at least one opinion about text content using appropriate agreement or evaluative language

nodes.label: Responding to cultural nuance, humour and diverse perspectives
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can respond to cultural nuance, humour and diverse community perspectives in target language texts, including First Nations Australian stories.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify cultural nuance or humour in at least one target language text and explain what cultural knowledge is needed to understand it; produce a culturally appropriate response.
nodes.typical_width: Respond to humour in target language texts and compare with Australian conventions; exchange material with target language community peers; listen to First Nations Australian authors' stories and respond in the target language; respond to texts from diverse target language communities; select response form appropriate to cultural context.
wider: Compare target language community and Australian expressions of humour in two texts — identify what cultural knowledge each assumes and explain what this reveals about each culture
Produce a response to a First Nations Australian author's story in the target language — addressing both content and cultural significance

response_modes.reason: Cultural nuance and humour awareness develops through encountering diverse text types and cultural contexts. Each new cultural text context reveals different aspects of the language-culture relationship.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Reading cultural nuance and humour in authentic texts is where intercultural competence becomes genuinely sophisticated — students are developing real-world cultural literacy.
success_criteria: Identifies cultural nuance or humour in a text and explains what cultural knowledge is required
Produces a response appropriate to the text's cultural context — not only its linguistic content
